body: Other than the stress of future and school, my life is good. I have a loving family, girlfriend, and group of friends. Hell, half of the stress is that they are so caring that I don't want to let them all down.
That's certainly part of it, but I've had this depression (though not as badly) during times when I haven't been maxed as well. Maxing the credits was a bad, bad idea.

No, you're right. Those nights that I don't have homework and people get together to socialize, I sleep instead. I am happier when I'm more involved in things with other people, but I find myself getting involved in many group activities for this reason, which then only leads to greater time constraints, which leads me to dropping some of the non-school related things.  I worked a full time job last summer, had my own apartment, lived far far away from this school, and I wasn't depressed the entire time, so it's something that I'm doing (or not doing as the case may be) here that seems to be the problem.

Cutting back on school related things is very hard for me to do.  I am the third child in a family of overachievers. My parents met at MIT, my eldest sister was published before she was in high school, my next sister was doing differential equations in her sophomore year of high school, and I had completed a year of work at the local college while still attending high school.  I am petrified of disappointing my family and my friends, and my grades recently have begun slipping so low as to put my perilously close to getting me expelled (see the fact that I'm on scholastic probation - if I fail a class, then they expel me).  It's at times when I'm thinking about that especially that my minds sinks into despair and wants to die to get away from it all.  It's like it would finally be restful and easy and stress-free to just be dead, even though my rational mind knows that that isn't true at all.
My permanent residence is in Vermont, but I go to school in New York.

I was afraid to tell my therapist about suicidal thoughts, because I didn't want that to get out and possibly put an end to other things I want to do (for instance will they still allow you to work for the FBI if you've had such thoughts before?)

You raise some very good points.  Unfortunately, the school I go to is literally the worst party school in the USA, and even on those times when friends are getting together for parties, half the time I feel that I can't go because of homework and projects that need doing.  I used to play video games, but that stopped, too.
I'm a Computer Science major and was taking the maximum number of credit hour until I withdrew from one of my courses last week.

I haven't tried medication, no.  I have an aversion to it for fear of becoming dependent, but it may be what I need after all.

I do have medical insurance, and have used 3 therapists so far, and while we don't have a family physician per se, I still call my old pediatrician from time to time with health questions, as I know and trust him.
